investigator.note: I prioritised regional earthquakes (over 200 M5.5+ historical events), extreme rainfall and flooding (multiple heavy rain days and GDACS flood/cyclone alerts), and localized gas explosions (2007 Shibuya methane explosion). For flooding and heavy rainfall, I checked low-lying block exposure, land cover change, and walking access to elevated flood refuges. For earthquake and gas explosion safety, I assessed proximity to industrial sites and walking access to major hospitals, open ground assembly points, underground shelters, and veterinary clinics for animal readiness.

report.summary: Shibuya faces risks from earthquakes, extreme rainfall, and urban gas leaks. Flood refuges and open ground assembly points are widely accessible, but walking access to major hospitals within the 3 km zone is severely limited. Addressing major hospital access and flood gaps in low-lying blocks are top priorities.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: Over 200 earthquakes of M5.5+ occurred within 200 km since 1970.

matrix.finding: 82.2% of residents are within 500 m walking distance of an underground shelter (median walk distance 305 m).
98.4% of residents are within 500 m walking distance of open ground assembly points.
0.0% of residents have a major hospital mapped within 500 m or 1000 m (median walk distance is 3150 m). No major hospital is mapped within 3 km.
23.0% of residents live within 500 m of a veterinary clinic, while median walk distance is 977 m.
No specific post-earthquake nature monitoring dataset available.

readiness.why_it_matters_here: 36.8% of blocks (32 blocks with 37777 residents) are low-lying and susceptible to heavy rainfall events.

matrix.finding: 2 low-lying blocks with 2337 residents lack a flood refuge within 300 m.
97.6% of residents are within 500 m walk of a tall building flood refuge.
Water surface area dropped from 2.9% in 2016 to 1.7% in 2025, a reduction of 1.2 percentage points.

recommendations.what: Establish emergency medical transit corridors to major hospitals outside the 3 km area.
recommendations.why: 0.0% of residents are within 1000 m of a major hospital and median walk distance is 3150 m (up to 4865 m in Aobadai). No major hospital is mapped within 3 km.

recommendations.what: Designate and construct vertical flood refuges or elevated assembly zones.
recommendations.why: 2 low-lying blocks containing 2337 residents lack a flood refuge within 300 m.

recommendations.what: Improve veterinary care access and emergency animal shelter planning.
recommendations.why: Only 23.0% of residents are within 500 m of a vet clinic, and walking distance reaches 3331 m in Harajuku.
